clue.text: Item in account for which I'd no receipt-a correction needed

indicators.note: a correction needed says these letters are wrong as they stand and must be put into a new order

explanation.surface: A bookkeeper finds an entry with no receipt behind it and flags it for correcting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'correction needed' signals the anagram of I'D NO RECEIPT A; 'for which' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Depreciation is a recurring accounting entry recording the falling value of an asset.

clue.text: Figure seen a month since at the Nag's Head

parts.note: Dec is the short form of December
since, as in 'some time since', means ago

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so only the start of Nag's is used

explanation.surface: Someone was last seen a month back at a pub called the Nag's Head.
explanation.walkthrough: The Nag's Head is a common British pub name, so the surface reads as a missing-person report.
explanation.definitionFit: A decagon is a plane shape with ten sides, a geometric figure.

clue.text: Headgear for eccentric peers all round the realm

indicators.note: all round says the shuffled letters surround the next piece
eccentric means odd or irregular, so the letters of peers are rearranged

parts.note: the United Kingdom, UK, is the realm

explanation.surface: Odd lords of the kingdom wearing their ceremonial headwear.
explanation.walkthrough: PEERS rearranged gives PERES, which 'all round' wraps about UK.
explanation.definitionFit: Perukes are the long wigs of the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, worn on the head.

clue.text: Annexe formerly fabricated in stone

parts.note: ex- as a prefix means former, as in ex-husband

indicators.note: fabricated means made up, so the letters of in stone are assembled anew

explanation.surface: A building annexe that used to be built of stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fabricated' turns IN STONE into TENSION.
explanation.definitionFit: An extension is an added wing or room built onto a house, an annexe.

clue.text: Rockall, say, has a tenant

definitions.meaning: Rockall is a tiny rocky outcrop in the North Atlantic, an example of a small island
a property that has a tenant ..., so it '...'

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits into two words: IS LET.
explanation.definitionFit: Rockall is a small isolated island in the Atlantic, and a rented house 'is let' when occupied by a lodger.

clue.text: Soldier's dog

definitions.meaning: informal British for a member of the Territorial Army, the volunteer reserve
a breed type of small hunting dog, like a Jack Russell

explanation.walkthrough: The Territorial Army is Britain's part-time volunteer reserve; its members were nicknamed Terriers.
explanation.definitionFit: A reservist of the Territorial Army is nicknamed after the small burrowing dog breed.

clue.text: Tedious opera girl deserted by artist

indicators.note: deserted by means left by, so the artist's letters go out of the string

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, the usual crossword artist
Rose is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A dull opera in which the leading lady is abandoned by a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: OPERA + ROSE makes OPERAROSE; 'deserted by' removes RA to leave the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Operose is a rare word meaning laborious, involving much toil and effort.

clue.text: Union demonstration ?

parts.note: reads like a trade union protest march, but union is marriage and the demonstration is a procession of music

explanation.walkthrough: Union here is a marriage, not a trade union, and the march is music, not a protest.
explanation.definitionFit: Mendelssohn's well-known processional is played as a bride and groom leave the church after their marriage.

clue.text: Right in leaving out the extract

indicators.note: in tells us the letter goes inside the other piece

parts.note: except means leaving out, as in 'all except him'

explanation.surface: Correctly omitting a passage from a text.
explanation.definitionFit: An excerpt is a passage taken out of a longer work, a quotation or extract.

clue.text: Such a mob as Pickwick advised Snodgrass to shout with

definitions.text: Such a mob as Pickwick advised Snodgrass to shout with

parts.words: Such a mob as Pickwick advised Snodgrass to shout with
parts.note: in Dickens's Pickwick Papers, asked what to do when there are two mobs at an election, Mr Pickwick tells Snodgrass to shout with the bigger one

explanation.walkthrough: The clue quotes The Pickwick Papers: at the Eatanswill election Pickwick says to do what the mob does, and with two mobs, 'Shout with the largest'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pickwick's advice names the crowd of greatest size, the superlative of big.

clue.text: Mason's hatter may provide them

indicators.note: the words may provide the letters, rearranged, from which the answer is made

parts.note: the possessive S is counted as a letter here

explanation.surface: A hat shop run by a Mason supplies headgear.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram 'may provide' uses all twelve letters of MASONS HATTER; and a hatter would indeed provide such caps.
explanation.definitionFit: Tam-o'-shanters are flat woollen Scottish bonnets, the sort of caps a hatter sells.

clue.text: Leather traces his family

parts.note: to trace someone is to follow them, to dog them
kin means one's family or relatives

explanation.surface: A leather-worker researching his family tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogskin is leather made from the hide of a dog, used for gloves.

clue.text: Having three styles in which to test class orally

indicators.note: orally means spoken, so the word for test is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to try is to test
a form is a school class

explanation.surface: A teacher with three different methods of examining a class by spoken questions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'orally' turns TRY into its sound-alike TRI, the prefix for three.
explanation.definitionFit: Triform means existing in three shapes or forms, so it has three styles.

clue.text: The Muses' style of dress?

parts.note: there were nine Muses, so their way of dressing is jokingly named after their number, as in the idiom for dressing very smartly

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'dressed to the nines' means very smartly dressed; the nine Muses of Greek myth turn it into a pun.
explanation.definitionFit: To dress to the nines is to dress elaborately, and nine was the number of the Muses.

clue.text: Send Rosie to change bills over to them

indicators.note: to change says these letters must be altered into another order

explanation.surface: Asking Rosie to send off some bills for them to be changed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' rearranges SEND ROSIE; indorsees are those to whom bills of exchange are signed over.
explanation.definitionFit: An indorsee is the person to whom a bill of exchange or cheque is legally transferred by signature.

clue.text: Defeat record order ? Well !

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
OM is the Order of Merit
fit means well, in good health

explanation.surface: Someone rejecting a record order, ending with an exclamation.
explanation.walkthrough: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: To discomfit is, in its older sense, to rout or overthrow an enemy.

clue.text: A thousand to one divine Heather's producing second-class goods

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
I is the Roman numeral for one
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a divine
ling is a name for heather, read here as the plural

explanation.surface: A woman named Heather bets a thousand to one and turns out mediocre goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather' looks like a woman's name but is the plant, ling. A divine is a clergyman, often a Doctor of Divinity.
explanation.definitionFit: Middlings are goods of medium grade, especially coarse flour, between best and worst.

clue.text: He takes Hazel to be more godly ?

definitions.meaning: a dowser walks with a forked hazel twig to find water underground
divine means godlike, so the comparative is more godlike

explanation.walkthrough: Hazel looks like a woman's name but is the twig a water-finder uses.
explanation.definitionFit: A water dowser uses a hazel rod, and the comparative of divine means more godlike.

clue.text: No exaggeration, for instance, to catch a child in untruths

indicators.note: to catch means to hold, so the untruths go around the child

parts.note: lies are untruths
a tot is a small child

explanation.surface: Not overstating things, as when a fibber catches a child out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to catch' puts TOT inside LIES. Litotes is understatement, such as 'not bad' for good, the opposite of exaggeration.
explanation.definitionFit: Litotes is ironic understatement, the figure of speech that is the reverse of hyperbole.

clue.text: Girl has drink in a ship? On the contrary

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
on the contrary swaps the order the words state, so it is the ship that goes into the drink

parts.note: tea is a drink
SS is steamship

explanation.surface: A girl who sips a drink aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, TEA goes in SS; 'On the contrary' reverses that, putting SS inside TEA.
explanation.definitionFit: Tessa is a female forename.

clue.text: A lot more shaky ? Yes

indicators.note: shaky means unsteady, so the letters of lot more are jumbled

explanation.surface: Asking whether something is much more unsteady and getting a firm yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shaky' rearranges LOT MORE; a tremolo is a trembling, wavering musical effect, so the whole clue is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tremolo is a quivering effect in music or singing, much more wavering in tone.

clue.text: Point to Erica's covers

parts.note: S, south, is a point of the compass
erica is the botanical name for heath, read as plural

explanation.surface: Indicating a woman named Erica's blankets.
explanation.walkthrough: Erica looks like a girl's name but is the plant genus of heaths.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheaths are close-fitting cases, protective covers for blades.

clue.text: Fixed a horse doctor in a rough ride

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other
rough means disordered, so the letters of ride are scrambled

parts.note: a vet treats animals, horses included

explanation.surface: A veterinary surgeon stuck on a horse during a bumpy ride.
explanation.walkthrough: RIDE rearranged as RIED takes VET inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Riveted means fastened with rivets, so held firmly in place.

clue.text: Does this benefactor then only do wrong?

definitions.text: Does this benefactor then only do wrong?

parts.words: Does this benefactor then only do wrong?
parts.note: the word for a giver can be split into two short words and R for right, so it seems to say he does nothing right

explanation.walkthrough: Split the five letters into two little words plus R, the abbreviation for right, and the giver appears to do no good at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A donor gives money or blood, a benefactor.

clue.text: How to wax fat-but nothing ever changes at last

parts.note: O, zero, is nothing

indicators.note: changes means alters, so the letters of ever are rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice on putting on weight, but nothing ever alters in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' turns EVER into VERE; AT comes last, as 'last' says.
explanation.definitionFit: To overindulge in food is the way to grow fat, waxing meaning growing.

clue.text: 8 from Neath on it on Devon Place

indicators.note: 8 points to the answer at 8-across, a passage taken out, so the place is a stretch extracted from the next words

explanation.surface: A clip of a Welsh town's report about somewhere in Devon.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer to 8-across means an extract, so '8 from' asks for letters taken from NEATH ON IT ON. Neath is a town in Wales; Devon is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Honiton is a market town in east Devon, famous for its lace.

clue.text: One who may change sides in Cork, perhaps ?

definitions.meaning: a floating voter or someone who drifts between parties
cork stays on the water's surface, an example of something buoyant

explanation.walkthrough: Cork looks like the Irish city but is the buoyant bark.
explanation.definitionFit: A voter who switches party allegiance, and a cork bobbing on water, both drift.

clue.text: Even making allowances after Flora's first blight, they are disappointing

indicators.note: after says the allowances come behind the earlier pieces
first picks only the opening letter of Flora's

parts.note: rust is a fungal plant blight
rations are fixed allowances

explanation.surface: Even with allowances made, Flora's first crop disease is a letdown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Even making' is link padding. Rust is a fungal disease of plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Frustrations are setbacks that thwart hopes, causing disappointment.
